ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows a common-emitter BJT amplifier. The input signal vi passes through coupling capacitor C and then a series 10 kΩ resistor to the transistor base; the transistor is labeled hfe = 100. The collector is connected through a 10 kΩ resistor to +Vcc, and vo is taken out through output coupling capacitor C. The emitter is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to ground, and a bypass capacitor C is connected in parallel across this 1 kΩ resistor. Reasoning: In the mid-frequency range, all coupling and bypass capacitors are regarded as short circuits, and +Vcc is AC-equivalent to ground. The emitter bypass capacitor AC-shorts the 1 kΩ emitter resistor, so the emitter is AC ground. According to the simplified small-signal model specified by the problem, the input base current ib = vi / 10 kΩ. The transistor collector current ic = hfe·ib = 100 ib. This collector current flows through the 10 kΩ collector resistor at the AC-grounded end, and the output voltage vo = -ic·10 kΩ. Therefore the voltage gain magnitude |vo/vi| = 100 × 10 kΩ / 10 kΩ = 100.

The emitter bypass capacitor shorts the 1 kΩ emitter resistor for AC, so the emitter is at AC ground. This current through the visible 10 kΩ collector resistor produces vo = -ic(10 kΩ). Therefore compute the magnitude |vo/vi| = 100 × 10 kΩ/10 kΩ = 100.
